items.sub: Fix: expect a multi-year craft, and the disappointment never comes.

items.h: They blew up by skipping risk rules
items.sub: Fix: 1% per trade, always. You can't quit if you're still standing.

items.h: They chased a new strategy every week
items.sub: Fix: master one simple edge before touching a second.

items.h: They couldn't sit through a drawdown
items.sub: Fix: paper trading builds the stomach before real money does.

items.h: They traded alone, in the dark
items.sub: Fix: journal, and learn beside honest people building in the open.

props.caption: Almost nobody quits because the math was too hard. They quit for these five reasons.

props.title: What success actually looks like

stats.label: of your effort is process, not prediction
one small, durable edge is a real career
shortcuts that actually work
stats.src: it's a craft, not a jackpot

props.note: The realistic win is a modest, repeatable edge you defend for years — not a jackpot.

props.title: Should you actually do this?

left.title: Do it if…
items: You love the process, not just profit
You'll treat it as a multi-year craft
You can risk money you won't miss
You enjoy coding and data puzzles

right.title: Skip it if…
items: You need this money to grow safely
A guaranteed-returns ad pulled you in
You won't paper trade patiently first

props.caption: For most people, low-cost index investing beats a home-made bot. That's okay.

props.title: A simple weekly routine

items.h: Check the logs — did the bot behave?
items.sub: Every trade should match a rule you can point to.

items.h: Compare live results to the backtest
items.sub: Drifting apart is your early warning of edge decay.

items.h: Review your journal, not just your P&L
items.sub: Did you override the bot? Why? Be honest with yourself.

items.h: Research one improvement — test it offline
items.sub: Never edit a live bot on a whim. Change it deliberately.

props.caption: The work is never 'set and forget'. It's a calm, weekly loop of checking and improving.
